clinical_category: Home oxygen discharge coordination - equipment and safety education
blueprint_topic: Discharge planning and caregiver preparation for home oxygen therapy
stem: A nurse prepares a client and caregiver for discharge with prescribed home oxygen. Which action is an essential part of this discharge preparation?

options.A: Provide instruction and training on oxygen-equipment use and maintenance and on oxygen safety
options.B: Arrange oxygen delivery but omit equipment teaching because the prescription alone is sufficient
options.C: Teach only the client and exclude the caregiver from equipment and safety education
options.D: Limit teaching to the oxygen flow setting and omit fire and fall-hazard precautions

rationale: A is correct. The official ATS home-oxygen guideline includes a best-practice statement recommending that patients prescribed home oxygen and their caregivers receive instruction and training on the use and maintenance of all oxygen equipment and education on oxygen safety, including fire prevention and tripping hazards. B, C, and D omit required elements of that best-practice statement. The source item's broader claims about individualized equipment selection and durable-medical-equipment-provider coordination were removed because the selected guideline locator directly supports education, equipment use/maintenance, and safety.
educational_objective: Include both the client and caregiver in instruction on home-oxygen equipment use, maintenance, and safety as part of discharge preparation.
source_document_title: Home Oxygen Therapy for Adults with Chronic Lung Disease: An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline
source_version_date: Official ATS guideline published 2020/2021 with erratum; currently listed by ATS and accessed 2026-08-18
source_locator: Education and Safety → ATS Recommendation / best-practice statement: patients prescribed home oxygen and their caregivers should receive instruction and training on adherence to the oxygen prescription, use, maintenance and troubleshooting of all oxygen equipment, and oxygen-safety education including smoking cessation, fire prevention, and tripping hazards.
source_claim_supported: The current official ATS guideline directly supports client-and-caregiver training in oxygen-equipment use/maintenance and oxygen-safety education as essential elements of home oxygen therapy.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care client-needs subcategory (15–21% of items), within Safe and Effective Care Environment; this item tests discharge planning, caregiver preparation, and coordination of safe home therapy.
correction_summary: Substantive rebuild. The generic AARC homepage was replaced with the official ATS home-oxygen guideline and its exact Education and Safety best-practice statement. The final item removes unlocated claims about DME-provider coordination and equipment selection and tests only directly supported discharge-teaching elements.
audit_findings: The original AARC root URL did not supply an exact home-oxygen coordination locator.
The official ATS guideline gives a direct best-practice statement requiring patient-and-caregiver oxygen-equipment and safety education.
The final item avoids unsupported universal claims about which DME provider must be used or how equipment must be selected in every case.
All distractors omit a directly required component of the ATS best-practice statement and are not defensible alternatives.
Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct answer, no second answer, no cueing, no unsupported flow-rate precision, and no unresolved conflict.
